A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, An Evolved Universal Transformer Memory, with 35 pages and complete Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical substantive content, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original NAMM experiments on language, video understanding and reinforcement learning, plus appendix ablations, timing measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including benchmark evaluations, ablations and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The attention-spectrogram features, EMA reduction, BAM architecture, token-eviction procedure and CMA-ES optimization are identical, including Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LongBench, InfiniteBench, ChouBun, LongVideoBench, MLVU and D4RL coverage, along with the Needle In A Haystack evaluation in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments. Full-cache models, H2O, L2, FastGen and the appendix comparison variants are neither added nor removed.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, context handling, sampling procedures and evaluation metrics remain identical in Section 3.3 and Appendices A–C.

E4.justification: The architecture, incremental-training and feature ablations, cache-size sweeps, gradient analyses, qualitative examples and sparse-retrieval sensitivity experiment are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same CMA-ES population means and standard deviations and average reinforcement-learning evaluation over 20 random seeds (Figure 4; Appendix A.3). No uncertainty-reporting or run-count information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including NAMM's InfiniteBench overall score of 11.00 in Table 3 and D4RL overall score of 31.73 in Table 7. Appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(6), including attention, STFT, EMA and gradient analysis, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and Section 6 retain identical claims about learned KV-cache management, performance and efficiency benefits, and zero-shot transfer across architectures and modalities.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are identical, including cross-token competition, generalization explanations, sparse-retrieval failures and the constraint imposed by requiring explicit attention values.

D1.justification: Appendix A implementation details, Table 9 hyperparameters, Appendix C.5 hardware and timing disclosures, and stated code/data access information are unchanged. Embedded link targets also match.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix E and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to heuristic cache eviction, efficient transformer architectures and evolutionary methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint, under review' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'. The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 6 Dec 2024 to v4 dated 13 Feb 2025. Body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 16 figures, 24 tables, captions and page-body layouts are identical. The publication-header and arXiv-stamp text updates are editorial changes recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: v4 updates publication-status and version metadata, while retaining identical methods, evidence, explanations and limitations throughout the main paper and appendices. These editorial updates do not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
